grades.requirement:
Start by identifying the major services competing for viewers in South Korea. The goal is to understand the actual market structure before comparing individual platforms.

Begin with official company and platform sources, then use industry research to identify significant services that may not appear prominently in international searches.

Investigate categories including:

Global subscription streaming platforms
Korean streaming platforms
Broadcaster-owned streaming services
Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) and online TV services
Advertising-supported streaming or FAST services, where available
Live TV and catch-up services

Start with platforms and organizations such as:

https://www.netflix.com/kr-en
https://www.wavve.com
https://www.coupangplay.com
https://www.disneyplus.com/ko-kr
https://watcha.com
https://www.kcc.go.kr
https://www.kca.kr

Search for additional relevant platforms through Korean media-industry reporting, company announcements, and official broadcaster websites.

Create a market map containing approximately 10–15 significant services or distribution ecosystems.

For each, record:

Service	Operator/Owner	Service Type	Main Content	Free/Paid Model	Korean Market Focus

Deduplicate services that are simply different access points to the same underlying product.

Do not automatically treat every global streaming service as a major local competitor. Look for evidence that the service is actually active and relevant in South Korea.

Output

Produce a South Korean streaming and online TV market map containing 10–15 significant platforms or service ecosystems.
grades.reasoning: The agent conducted a thorough search of the South Korean streaming landscape, gathering information on major global players (Netflix, Disney+), local dominant services (Tving, Coupang Play, Wavve), and niche/smaller services (Laftel, Watcha). It also gathered details on market structure, regulation, and IPTV bundling. However, the agent failed to synthesize this information into the required market map (a list/table of 10-15 services with specific columns: Service, Operator/Owner, Service Type, Main Content, Free/Paid Model, Korean Market Focus). The agent only performed searches and reviewed snippets without compiling the final deliverable.

grades.requirement:
Using the market map, investigate who operates each platform and how the major players obtain or control content.

For every significant platform:

Open its official company or service information.
Identify the operating company and parent organization.
Determine whether the service is:
Independent
Broadcaster-owned
Telecommunications-owned
E-commerce or technology-company-owned
International
Investigate major broadcaster, studio, sports, telecommunications, or production partnerships.
Identify evidence of exclusive content, original productions, or distribution agreements.

Use:

Official company announcements
Investor relations pages
Regulatory filings where applicable
Official broadcaster and production-company announcements

For major Korean broadcasters, inspect their corporate and digital distribution pages to understand relationships between television networks and streaming services.

Create an ownership and content-control table:

Platform	Operating Company	Parent/Key Owner	Major Partners	Original/Exclusive Content Strategy	Verification Source
Decision constraint

Do not assume that a platform owns content simply because it streams it.

Separate:

Owned intellectual property
Original productions
Licensed exclusives
Non-exclusive licensed content
Live or catch-up broadcaster content
Output

Produce a verified ownership and content-strategy map showing the relationships between platforms, broadcasters, telecommunications companies, and content producers.
grades.reasoning: The agent conducted a series of Google searches to gather information on the South Korean OTT market, including platform ownership (e.g., Coupang Play, TVING, Wavve), competitive strategies, and regulatory environment. However, the agent failed to create the requested "ownership and content-control table" or the "verified ownership and content-strategy map" required by the rubric. While it gathered some individual components of the data, the synthesis and final output required by the rubric are completely absent from the action history.

Ecosystem-based access

1. Select 8–10 of the most significant services.
2. Open the pricing/membership pages for each platform to investigate subscription tiers, advertising, video quality, simultaneous streams, etc.

The agent performed Google searches and relied on AI-generated summary snippets rather than visiting the official platform pages (e.g., Netflix, TVING, Wavve, Disney+, Coupang Play websites) to verify tier details, device compatibility, or specific business model constraints. grades.requirement:
Now investigate how Korean audiences are actually using streaming and online TV.

Use authoritative and reputable sources such as:

https://www.kocca.kr/kocca/main.do
https://www.kcc.go.kr
https://www.kca.kr
https://datareportal.com
Company investor reports
Official or established media-industry research

Research indicators such as:

Streaming adoption
Online video consumption
Mobile versus television viewing
Popular content categories
Domestic versus international content demand
Sports and live-content consumption
Subscription fatigue or multi-service usage
Advertising-supported viewing

Where market-share or usage figures are obtained from third-party research, record:

The source
Methodology if available
Reporting period
Whether the figure measures subscribers, monthly active users, viewing time, app usage, or another metric

Do not combine different metrics as though they represent the same measurement.

Create an audience and positioning table:

Platform	Available Audience Metric	Measurement Type	Core Audience Position	Content Strength	Source/Period
Output

Produce an audience-demand and competitive-positioning analysis that distinguishes verified metrics from broader market observations.
grades.reasoning: The agent conducted extensive research across multiple search queries regarding the South Korean streaming market, including usage rates, MAU (Monthly Active Users), subscription pricing, regulatory environments, and content strategies. Screenshots show the agent gathering specific data points, such as MAU figures from Wiseapp (Screenshot 13), usage rates from the KCC (Screenshot 3), and subscription pricing tiers for various platforms (Screenshot 5). However, the agent failed to create the requested "audience and positioning table." The instructions explicitly required the agent to "Create an audience and positioning table" with specific columns (Platform, Available Audience Metric, Measurement Type, Core Audience Position, Content Strength, Source/Period). Because this final required output component was missing from the trajectory, the rubric requirement was not fully satisfied.

Telecommunications or broadcasting classifications where relevant

The official regulations or guidance that appear relevant.
Areas where a new entrant would likely need legal or regulatory confirmation.

Then investigate the distribution environment:

Smart TV ecosystems
Local telecommunications companies
Broadband/IPTV relationships
Device partnerships
App-store availability

Create a market-entry constraint table:

Area	Relevant Authority/Platform	Verified Requirement or Issue	Potential Business Impact	Requires Specialist Confirmation?

The trajectory consists entirely of search queries and reading AI-generated summaries from Google; it never synthesized the requested deliverables or accessed the authoritative government websites specified in the instructions.

Official platform and company sources
Broadcaster and telecommunications sources
Industry research
Secondary media reporting

For every major conclusion, retain the underlying source so the research can be revisited and updated.
